newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB willing to be diluted in Tractebel -Electrabel.
newsitem.headline: SGB willing to be diluted in Tractebel -Electrabel.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) said on Wednesday it had no objection to a possible merger of its utility units Electrabel NV and Tractebel SA.
An SGB spokesman told Reuters SGB was willing to see its stake in a future, merged Tractebel-Electrabel diluted to below 50 percent as long as it remained the controlling shareholder.
SGB currently has 65 percent of Tractebel. That will fall to just over 50 percent in October when Tractebel finalises a merger with its foreign energy unit Powerfin.
"We are not against a merger between Tractebel and Electrabel, provided this is beneficial for both companies and all its shareholders," the SGB spokesman said.
"We would be willing to accept a dilution below 50 percent in the new unit as long as we remain the controlling shareholder," he added.

He added that if the Belgian government wanted to merge Tractebel and Electrabel, this should mean an end to regulation in the electricity sector. "A merger should mean the end of the official fixing of electricity prices."
At present the electricity sector is highly regulated, notably via the fixing of electricity prices by the government.
The spokesman declined to say whether deregulation was a condition for SGB's approval of a merger. "This is a condition for the liberalisation of the market in Europe," he said.
Last December the 15 European Union member states agreed to liberalise 12 percent of their electricity markets by 1999, rising to 33 percent by 2003.
